featured.title: Tracking the shifts shaping AI silicon, advanced packaging, and next-generation manufacturing.
featured.description: A curated snapshot of what major semiconductor players are pushing right now, from AI compute platforms and packaging ecosystems to foundry economics and manufacturing scale.

chips.title: Advanced Packaging
chips.text: Chiplets, dense interconnects, and system-level integration remain central to performance scaling.

chips.title: AI Silicon
chips.text: Model growth is pushing every layer of the stack, from GPUs and CPUs to memory and power delivery.

chips.title: Foundry Race
chips.text: Capacity, node execution, and ecosystem readiness are still the decisive variables for scale.

items.title: Intel highlighted open, scalable AI performance in MLPerf Inference v6.0.
items.summary: The signal here is broader than a benchmark score: Intel is continuing to position its AI stack around openness, deployability, and heterogeneous compute across enterprise workloads.

items.title: NVIDIA expanded its AI ecosystem through NVLink Fusion with Marvell.
items.summary: This reinforces the direction of tightly integrated AI infrastructure, where interconnect strategy, platform alliances, and system architecture matter as much as raw accelerator performance.

items.title: TSMC and Samsung remain central to the discussion around node leadership, advanced packaging, and manufacturing resilience.
items.summary: For engineers, the practical takeaway is clear: process maturity, packaging capacity, yield learning, and ecosystem support are increasingly inseparable from product competitiveness.

items.title: Power efficiency is now a first-order design story, not a secondary optimization.
items.summary: NVIDIA's recent discussion around power-flexible AI factories reflects an industry-wide reality: future compute growth depends on energy-aware architecture, packaging, cooling, and deployment economics.
